title: AI in education
lede: In two years generative AI went from novelty to daily habit: most teens now use chatbots for schoolwork and most teachers use AI for their jobs. Guidance, training and evidence lag far behind use. The 2026–27 school year opens with the nation's two largest districts pulling student-facing AI back while Google, OpenAI and Anthropic push classroom tools out.

blocks.title: What the learning evidence says
blocks.subtitle: Rigorous studies of AI in instruction, newest first. Effect sizes are in standard deviations (SD) unless noted; 0.10 SD is roughly a few months of typical learning.

cells: Khanmigo AI tutor in middle-school math (Oreopoulos & Low, NBER, Aug 2026)
Two-year cluster RCT, 18 Tennessee middle schools, daily remedial math; tutor set to coach, not answer

+1.3 national percentile ranks per term (≈0.06–0.08 SD per year; 0.14 SD implied for a full year of active use). Gains resemble Khan practice without AI. Median student messaged the tutor on a third of practice days and in 17% of sessions with a mistake.
AI assistance on math and reading tasks (Liu et al., May 2026)
AI help raised in-task performance but cut study time and reduced persistence and performance on later unassisted tasks: faster completion, less learning.
Students' own accounts (RAND American Youth Panel, Mar 2026)
Use for homework rose from 48% to 62% during 2025; 67% believe heavy use harms critical thinking. RAND urges rules that separate 'cognitive offloading' from 'cognitive augmentation'.
RCT with ~900 human tutors and 1,800 K-12 students; AI assists the tutor in real time
+4 percentage points in topic mastery overall; up to +9 points for students of lower-rated tutors. About $20 per tutor per year.
Generative AI Can Harm Learning (Bastani et al., 2024)
RCT, ~1,000 high-school math students in Türkiye
Unrestricted GPT-4 raised practice scores 48% but exam scores fell 17% when access was removed; a guardrailed 'GPT Tutor' (+127% on practice) showed no exam harm.

items.note: Three-quarters say school discussed AI rules; just over half were taught how to use AI safely. Nearly half have never discussed AI safety with a parent.

items.note: 29% of teachers say the same. 86% of students and 85% of teachers used AI in 2024–25; half of students used it for school.

items.note: English-language submissions to Turnitin's detector; the company stresses scores are probabilistic, not verdicts. Half of students worry about false accusations (RAND).

items.headline: The White House made AI education a priority.
items.detail: Executive Order 14277 (April 23, 2025) created a Task Force on AI Education and the Presidential AI Challenge. The first challenge drew 20,000+ students from all 50 states; six national champion teams were honored June 9, 2026.

items.headline: States moved from guidance to law in 2026.
items.detail: 35 states plus Puerto Rico have official K-12 AI guidance. New 2026 laws include Oregon's design rules for minors (SB 1546), Washington's harm-reporting requirement (HB 2225), Virginia's guidance-and-training mandate (SB 394), Maryland's teacher PD (SB 720) and Utah's middle-school AI literacy standards (HB 273).

items.headline: Companion chatbots got their first rulebooks.
items.detail: California's SB 243 (effective Jan 1, 2026) requires disclosure, self-harm protocols and three-hour break reminders for minors; 12 states had companion-chatbot laws by mid-2026.

items.headline: The AFT built a $23M training academy with the labs.
items.detail: The National Academy for AI Instruction (Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, UFT) offers free AI training to all 1.8 million AFT members, starting with New York City educators in fall 2025.

items.headline: Public support is cooling.
items.detail: PDK found support for teachers using AI to prepare lessons fell to 49% (62% in 2024) and for AI tutoring to 60% (65%); 68% of parents oppose giving student data to AI software.

items.headline: New York City paused student-facing AI through 8th grade.
items.detail: A one-year moratorium for 2026–27 covers 2-K through grade 8, nearly 600,000 students; AI features are switched off in the classroom tools they use, with exceptions for students with disabilities and English learners. High schoolers get twice-yearly AI critical-thinking modules and limited pilots.

items.headline: Los Angeles followed within days.
items.detail: LAUSD restricted generative AI on district devices for all students for 2026–27 while a new ad hoc committee drafts guardrails, due by the end of the school year. It follows a June vote limiting classroom screen time.

items.headline: Google turned Gemini on for students of all ages.
items.detail: Since August 10, 2026, Gemini in Google Classroom is available to K-12 students whose admins enable it, not only those 18 and older. EdWeek reports schools were 'caught flat-footed', and Common Sense had flagged age-inappropriate responses in January.

items.headline: The labs are courting teachers directly.
items.detail: Anthropic launched a free Claude for Teachers tier for verified U.S. K-12 educators on July 14, 2026 and a district-managed tier on August 28, with no training on teacher data. OpenAI offers ChatGPT for Teachers free to verified U.S. K-12 educators through June 2027.

items.headline: AI literacy is becoming routine.
items.detail: Nearly 8 in 10 educators say high schoolers in their district get lessons on what AI is and how to use it responsibly, according to an EdWeek Research Center survey of 499 teachers, principals and district leaders.
